title: Pacific Gas and Electric panned after Homecoming weekend
body: Pacific Gas and Electric played at Western as part of Homecoming weekend in October 1970. Ernie Hearion reviewed the show in the Herald of 13 October under the heading "Utilities Down Sharply on Entertainment Market", and the 1971 Talisman said the group won over very few of the crowd. The same yearbook recorded that the Herald was outspoken that year about the entertainment on which the Associated Students chose to spend students' activity funds.

src.label: College Heights Herald 50:13, 13 Oct 1970 (review); 1971 Talisman, Homecoming and Concerts

why: Cut 13 October as the concert date, since that is the review's publication date and the Talisman places the show in Homecoming weekend, and demoted the date to October 1970 with the day unknown; replaced the Talisman quotation with a paraphrase and added the sourced line about Associated Students entertainment spending, which is the only student government tie any source gives.

title: Reginald Glass signs the Associated Students' entertainment contracts
body: The 1972 Talisman photographed Reginald Glass, vice-president of Associated Students, signing a speaker contract, and said signing contracts for concerts and speakers was one of his responsibilities. The first speaker the Associated Students sponsored was Dr Benjamin Spock. Its other activities that year included bringing in the Trinidad Steel Band, Ike and Tina Turner and several mini-concerts, sponsoring the Homecoming dance, and running a mock election before the Kentucky governor's race.
why: Cut the block-booking and high-prices views, which are not in the 1972 Talisman, and the unsourced claim that Glass was the first black vice president; kept the caption the source does carry and added the list of Associated Students entertainment on the same pages.

title: Edmund Muskie calls for Nixon's impeachment in an ASG lecture
body: ASG sponsored the lecture Senator Edmund Muskie of Maine gave at Western on 11 December 1973, on the restoration of confidence in government. Muskie called for the impeachment of President Nixon, saying he had decided on the night of the Saturday Massacre that impeachment was the only way the issue should be raised. He cited a Harris poll in which 19 per cent of Americans said they had confidence in the executive branch. The 1974 Talisman lists Muskie with Barry Goldwater and Elliot Richardson among the lectures ASG sponsored that year.

src.label: 1974 Talisman, pp. 52-55 (Lectures); date from College Heights Herald 53:26, 4 Dec 1973

why: The cited Herald issue is only an advance notice, so the substance now rests on the 1974 Talisman, which I read and which carries the ASG sponsorship, the topic, the impeachment call and the Harris poll figure; the Herald keeps only the 11 December date.

title: Pure Prairie League: sound ruins the first show, the second is far better
body: Associated Student Government billed Pure Prairie League, and the group played two shows in Van Meter on 31 January 1975. Sound problems ruined most of the first act at 7:30, and the bassist, printed in the Talisman as Mike Rieley, asked the 9:30 audience whether anyone had seen the first show. He said it was the group's first experience with the sound crew the university had contracted. The problems were solved before the second show, which the 1975 Talisman rated far better.

src.label: 1975 Talisman, Entertainment; announced in College Heights Herald 50:31, 24 Jan 1975

why: The Herald citation was an advance notice, so the review now rests on the 1975 Talisman, which I read and which supplies the 31 January date and the two shows, while ASG's billing comes from the Herald headline; the bassist's name is left as the Talisman prints it, Rieley, and a caption elsewhere in the same volume misdates this concert to 30 October.

title: ASG's promoter had not signed a contract days before the Player and Exile concert
body: ASG said in the early autumn of 1978 that it would sign a contract with Sunshine Promotions, an Indianapolis concert firm, and its activities vice president David Carwell said the company met the three requirements for an outside promoter: an office within 500 miles of Western, at least 75 major concerts promoted, and $2 million grossed on them. Eight days before the Player and Exile concert of 3 November, the Herald reported that Western had still not signed, because the firm would not post the $100,000 performance bond the university required to guarantee that all the bills would be paid. Sunshine's Sybesma said Indiana insurance companies wanted 100 per cent collateral and a $2,000 service fee for the bond, and said his company might instead put up money before each concert. Sunshine later posted an irrevocable letter of credit that Western could cash if the concert bills went unpaid.

src.label: College Heights Herald 54:19, 26 Oct 1978; 1979 Talisman, Associated Student Government section

why: Cut the closing claim that the concert went ahead on an oral agreement, which belongs to the 9 November editorial and not to this issue, and softened 'refused to sign' to the firm's refusal to post the bond; added the ASG tie, the three promoter requirements, the Indiana insurers and the letter of credit from the 1979 Talisman, which I read.

title: ASG prepares to host the second statewide student government conference
body: The Herald reported on 26 March 1987 that ASG would be host, from the following day through Sunday, to the second annual statewide student government conference, at the American Plaza on Scottsville Road. President Tim Todd expected about 50 student leaders, against about 65 at the first conference, which ASG had also hosted, and said hosting would cost between $400 and $500. Registration was $18 and the conference was open to all students. Saturday seminars were to cover leadership, communication and financial aid, with the Council on Higher Education flying in a financial aid consultant from Washington and sending its director, Gary S. Cox.
why: Rewritten as the announcement the source actually is and redated from the conference weekend to the 26 March issue; I checked the issues either side, 62:47 of 24 March and 62:50 of 2 April, and found no report of how the weekend went, so nothing here says the conference took place.

title: Project Western Week and the planned Don't Trash The Spirit clean-up
body: SGA's Project Western Week began on Monday 8 February 1993 and ran through the week. Its biggest part was to be a mass campus clean-up the next day under the motto Don't Trash The Spirit. President Joe Rains said students would start picking up trash at about 3:30 p.m. at the New Co-Ed and New Sorority dorms, spread out across the width of campus and finish at Cherry Hall, and about 600 people were expected. The campus was to be divided into 23 sections taken by organisations that had until 5 February to sign up and that would stay responsible for their areas until the end of the semester, with $500 from SGA for the group keeping the cleanest area.
money: $500 prize to the organisation with the cleanest area
why: Recast the 10 February clean-up as announced rather than reported and redated the entry to the 8 February start of Project Western Week, which the source does give in the past tense; I checked the next issue, 68:36 of 11 February, and it carries no follow-up on the clean-up.

title: SGA sets a Dialogue Day with administrators
body: President Smith told the SGA meeting of 29 March 1994 that 6 April would be Dialogue Day, when students could talk with administrators in Niteclass from noon to 2 p.m. The public relations committee handed out flyers for it alongside flyers for the coming election. The same minutes record that security phones were expected to be in place by 26 April, and report on the memorial tree programme.
why: Redated from 6 April to the 29 March minutes and rewritten as the announcement they contain, since nothing shows the event took place; also dropped the 'run of access events' framing and the president's first name, which the minutes do not give. The 12 April 1994 minutes exist on TopSCHOLAR at sga/Meetings/Minutes/501 but the archive refused the PDF, so the event is still unconfirmed.

title: Herald reports SGA giving students rides
body: The Herald of 23 January 1997 carried Matt Batcheldor's report that the Student Government Association was giving rides to students. The archive's index of the issue records the article's title and byline and nothing more about the service.

src.label: College Heights Herald 72:31, 23 Jan 1997 - Batcheldor, "Student Government Association Gives Rides to Students"

why: Corrected the issue number from 72:29 to 72:31, which the record confirms, and cut everything the source does not carry: the name Provide-A-Ride, the January 1997 start, and the Herald warning a week later. SGA's own website described a free Provide-a-Ride van service on Thursday and Friday nights in a 2000 capture, but that does not date the start.

title: The last Congress meeting of the autumn, with the banquet to follow
body: SGA's website announced on 30 November 2003 that the banquet would be held right after the next Congress meeting, which would also be the last Congress meeting of the autumn semester. That meeting, the fourteenth of the year, was called to order at 5:05 p.m. on 2 December 2003 with 25 of the 43 members present, and the vice president of public relations, Abby Lovan, told it that a picture would be taken for the yearbook at the banquet.

src.label: WKU SGA Congress minutes, 2 Dec 2003, and SGA news page, 30 Nov 2003 (Wayback captures)

why: Dropped the claims that the banquet was held and the yearbook photograph taken, which no source reports, and moved the entry onto the 2 December minutes and the SGA news page, which I read and which give the meeting, its attendance and the plan for the photograph; the events calendar items the checker verified, Parents' Weekend lunch, the lighting and safety walk and the forums, are sound and belong in their own entries.

title: Senate funds a transcript voucher programme
body: The first bill passed at the SGA meeting on Tuesday 28 February 2012 allocated $1,225 for transcript vouchers, so that students applying for scholarships, jobs and graduate or professional school could get copies of their official transcripts free. A total of 175 vouchers were to be available, with a limit of two per student. A second bill put $500 of general senate funding into five $100 Study Away scholarships, and a further $2,300 went to Scholar Development Grant Awards and Study Abroad Awards. An organisational aid bill allocating $2,400 to five student groups had its first reading at the same meeting.
money: $1,225 for 175 vouchers; $500 in Study Away scholarships; $2,300 in grants; $2,400 organisational aid on first reading

src.label: College Heights Herald, 29 Feb 2012 - Taylor Harrison, "SGA to launch transcript voucher program"

why: Cut the $7 transcript price, the Cory Dodds quotation and Registrar Freida Eggleton, none of which appear in the article, which I read in full; added the organisational aid bill it does report and the author's name.

title: The Emme Kemp Jazz Trio opens the ASG mini-concert season
body: The Herald reported on 31 August 1971 that the Kemp Trio had set a concert. The 1972 Talisman recorded that the Associated Students entertained students with several mini-concerts that fall semester, small-scale shows meant to give top quality entertainment at less cost and presented in cooperation with other Kentucky colleges, and that the season started with the Emme Kemp Jazz Trio; student requests then brought the Trinidad Steel Band back with the Serendipity Singers.
why: Removed the invented 2 September concert date and dated the entry to the Herald issue that reports the booking; the mini-concert framing is now attributed in the body to the 1972 Talisman, which I read at archive.org/details/talisman1972west and which is the only source that ties the series to the Associated Students.

title: ASG announces a paper recycling project
body: The Herald of 6 October 1972 reported that Associated Student Government would launch a paper recycling project. The 1973 Talisman recorded that the project ran: paper was collected in ecology trash cans set at points across campus, collection was later extended to cans and bottles, and the money from the sale of recycled paper went back into the work of the Environmental Committee, which Joe Cheak headed.
why: Recast the cited article as the announcement it is, fixed the citation label to Vol. 52 No. 12, and attributed the ecology cans, the cans and bottles, the proceeds and Joe Cheak in the body to the 1973 Talisman, which I verified at archive.org/details/talisman1973west.

title: ASG books its fall entertainment fare
body: The Herald reported on 30 August 1974 that Associated Student Government had booked its entertainment programme for the fall semester. The 1975 Talisman set out the season that followed: an ASG bluegrass festival on 28 August, moved indoors to Van Meter Auditorium by rain and headlined by Lester Flatt and the Clinch Mountain Clan; Doc Severinsen at Homecoming on 11 October, picketed by about 30 students; and America free on 7 November. ASG had booked Al Stewart for a 3 November mini-concert, but his United States tour was cancelled over immigration law and activities vice-president Tom LaCivita booked Kiss in his place.
why: Cut the claim that Kiss and the rest were on the slate announced in August; the 1975 Talisman (archive.org/details/talisman1975west), now named in the body, shows Kiss was LaCivita's November replacement for the cancelled Al Stewart date, so the entry separates what the Herald reported on 30 August from the season the yearbook records.

title: Linda Ronstadt's Homecoming concert nets ASG $4,300
body: Linda Ronstadt played the Homecoming concert in Diddle Arena on Saturday 1 November 1975, opening with "Colorado", with Goose Creek Symphony before her and Andrew Gold as her backup group. The 1976 Talisman put the crowd at about 6,500 and the profit to ASG at $4,300, and reported that activities vice-president Rick Kelley and ASG president Steve Henry rated it among the most successful concerts in years - successful enough, the yearbook said, to guarantee a free Spinners and Wet Willie concert for students on 30 January.
money: netted $4,300 for ASG; attendance about 6,500, though the same yearbook's opening section gives 6,300
why: Moved the citation off the 31 October advance notice, which cannot carry an attendance or a profit, onto the 1976 Talisman where every figure and quotation actually appears, and flagged the yearbook's own conflicting 6,300 attendance figure.

title: James Taylor plays a free concert to close the year
body: The Herald of 20 April 1976 billed James Taylor for a free concert that Friday, and the issue of 23 April told readers the performance would be that night. The next issue, 27 April, carried Tip Shanklin's review under the headline "Evening with James Taylor Well Spent", so the concert took place. The 1976 Talisman listed James Taylor among the year's concerts but, before the event, recorded only that he was scheduled to give a free concert in April.
why: Cut Henry Gross and the 'big success' follow-up, which no source seen supports, and rescued the entry by finding the review in Herald 51:58 (27 Apr 1976), which confirms the show happened; no source seen names ASG as the booker, so the entry does not claim one.

title: Gerald O'Neill on space colonies
body: Gerald O'Neill, a physics professor at Princeton and author of "The High Frontier", told 100 people in the Center Theater in his lecture of 2 April 1979 that space colonies and solar power stations were possible with current technology, and that electricity from solar cells could be sent back to Earth as low energy microwaves. He said plans for space colonies existed but President Carter had abolished the NASA office exploring space colonisation, and that he was concerned about the militarisation of space because Carter had signed a bill to develop a particle beam weapon to be placed in space. The same yearbook records that lectures and concerts had been run by Associated Student Government until the Board of Regents voted on 31 March 1979 to hand that programming to a new University Center Board from the following autumn.

src.label: 1979 Talisman, Lectures p. 97 and University Center Board p. 81

why: Cut the $2,000 fee and the flat claim that ASG signed him, neither of which is in the cited Talisman, and replaced them with the same volume's statement that ASG ran lectures and concerts until the University Center Board took over; note the Talisman spells him Gerald O'Neill, so the spelling of the first name is unverified here.

title: Discount cards arrive, but do not go out
body: The ASG discount cards reached campus the day before the Herald's report of 1 October 1981. There were 14,000 of them and they offered students discounts at 21 listed merchants, valid until 1 September 1982. They were not handed out: Bush had been busy with other projects and passed the job to the communications committee, whose chairwoman, Laura Simms, was still working on a plan.
why: Corrected a misread: the article says ASG did not yet know how the 14,000 cards would be distributed, not how many it had or what was on them, and gives the delay a different cause; also cut the six businesses and at least fifteen figures, which belong to the 29 September issue, not this one.

title: ASG sets up a Wednesday afternoon hotline
body: Student government set up a hotline for complaints and suggestions about the organisation. From Wednesday 26 October the ASG secretary was to answer the office line, 745-4354, from 1 to 4 p.m. every Wednesday, referring anything she could not answer to an executive officer. Public relations vice president Amos Gott said students could call at any time during the week but did not, and that with a set time people were more apt to call.
why: Reattributed the quotation from administrative vice president Adrian Smoot, who was quoted on the page about the vacant parliamentarian post, to public relations vice president Amos Gott, who actually said it, and moved the entry's date to the 20 October issue because 26 October was still a prospective start.

title: Judge-executive candidates invited to congress
body: Administrative vice-president Scott Sivley told congress on 12 October 1993 that the Warren County judge-executive candidates, Miller and Buchanon, would be guests at the meeting of 26 October. The same minutes record speakers from Head Start before congress that evening.
why: Redated to the meeting the minutes actually record and recast as an invitation, since nothing here shows the candidates appeared on 26 October, and cut the closing claim about state legislators questioned earlier in the term, which is not in this document.

title: SGA to enter a homecoming queen candidate
body: The Herald reported on 22 September 1994 that the Student Government Association would enter a candidate for homecoming queen.

src.label: College Heights Herald 70:9, 22 Sep 1994 - Quarles and Mitchell, "Student Government Association to Enter Queen Candidate"

why: Cut the People Poll, the editorial cartoon and the week of argument - that issue's poll and cartoon are on other subjects entirely - and the congress vote, which the headline does not establish; corrected the citation from 70:11 to Vol. 70 No. 9.

title: Organizational Aid pays out $6,200 to 41 groups
body: Bill 98-9-F divided the $6,200 budgeted for Organizational Aid among 41 student organisations, a list the committee settled in two meetings running to over six hours. Awards ran from a floor of $100 to the Residence Hall Association's $205, and reached groups from Free the Planet to the Jewish Student Organization.

src.label: SGA Bill 98-9-F, Organizational Aid Recipients, 27 Oct 1998 (TopSCHOLAR)

why: Corrected the recipient count from 26 to the 41 organisations the bill lists; the total, the six hours over two meetings, the $205 top award and the $100 floor all stand.

title: SGA sets a dinner with lawmakers
body: SGA set its Dine with the Decision Makers for the evening of 8 December 2009, from 4:30 to 6 p.m. in the Cupola Room of Downing University Center, so students could talk about higher education with elected officials over dinner. President Kevin Smiley said 25 students had signed up through an online RSVP, a number capped by the cost of the dinner, and that five legislators and Bowling Green mayor Elaine Walker would attend. The event came out of a decision by the Board of Student Body Presidents that autumn that Kentucky's public universities should each mount student lobbying events.
money: 25 students signed up; numbers capped by the cost of the dinner

src.label: College Heights Herald 85:24, 8 Dec 2009 - "SGA to dine with lawmakers"

why: The cited article is a same-day preview, so the body now says what SGA scheduled rather than what happened, and "first" is gone: the source never calls it the inaugural edition.

title: Associated Students co-sponsored the musical '1776'
body: The Herald of 6 October 1970 announced that the curtain would rise the next day on the Broadway musical '1776'. Writing in the 1971 Talisman, Associated Students president John Lyne listed the co-sponsorship of '1776' among the theatrical events his government had backed as it widened its work from entertainment into cultural programmes. The same yearbook places the performance among that week's Homecoming activities.
why: Cut Jeanne Jackson's 'best ever musical', which I could not find; the checker was wrong that the 1971 Talisman has no Lyne account, so I kept the co-sponsorship and sourced it to his signed president's report at https://archive.org/details/talisman1971west.

title: Associated Students rescheduled the Isaac Hayes concert
body: The Isaac Hayes concert set for 17 February 1972 fell through when Hayes had flu, and the 1972 Talisman records that Associated Students rescheduled it for 23 March. Stephanie Madison's review in the Herald of 28 March shows the rescheduled show went ahead.
why: Kept the 23 March date after all: the checker read only the Talisman's body text, but the photograph caption in the same yearbook states the concert was rescheduled by Associated Students for March 23 (https://archive.org/details/talisman1972west).

title: Jimmy Buffett played an ASG mini-concert
body: The Herald of 17 April 1973 billed a mini-concert by Jimmy Buffett for that Thursday. The 1973 Talisman records that Buffett came to campus on 19 April in levis and a cowboy shirt carrying two Martin guitars, and counts him among the two major concerts, three mini-concerts and Bluegrass Festival that ASG sponsored that spring semester.
why: The cited Herald item is only an advance notice, so I attributed the date, the clothes, the guitars and the ASG sponsorship to the 1973 Talisman concerts section, which I read and which supplies all four (https://archive.org/details/talisman1973west).

title: ASG broke even on the Bar-Kays mini-concert
body: The Herald of 25 October 1974 billed the Bar-Kays for a mini-concert that night. The 1975 Talisman records that ASG presented the seven-member group, the backing band on Isaac Hayes's 'Hot Buttered Soul' and 'Shaft' albums, as one of its major mini-concerts of the year, and that ASG broke even on the concert.
why: Kept the money claim but moved it off the advance notice and onto the 1975 Talisman entertainment section, which I read and which states ASG broke even (https://archive.org/details/talisman1975west).

title: ASG sponsored Natalie Cole in Van Meter
body: The Herald reported on 9 December 1975 that Associated Student Government would sponsor a concert by the jazz vocalist Natalie Cole. The 1976 Talisman records that Cole, daughter of the late Nat King Cole, performed in Van Meter Auditorium on 10 December to an estimated crowd of 325, singing 'This Will Be', 'Killing Me Softly With His Song', 'Honky Tonk Women' and 'You Are the Sunshine of My Life'.
why: Left the ASG sponsorship on the cited advance notice and attributed the date, venue, crowd of 325 and songs to the 1976 Talisman, which I read and which carries all of them (https://archive.org/details/talisman1976west).

title: Jimmy Buffett and the Coral Reefer Band closed the concert year
body: The Herald announced on 25 March 1977 that a Jimmy Buffett concert was set for 27 April. The 1977 Talisman records that Buffett and the Coral Reefer Band played Diddle Arena that night, drawing three encores after a ninety-minute set from a small crowd, with highlights from 'Changes in Latitudes, Changes in Attitudes' and tunes from 'Livin' and Dyin' in 3/4 Time', 'A-1-A' and 'Havana Daydreamin''. The concert lost money, and the yearbook counts Buffett among the acts brought to Western in 1976-77 by the ASG concert programme run by activities vice president Rick Kelley.
why: Attributed the setlist and everything else about the night to the 1977 Talisman, which I read and which also supplies the ASG tie the checker could not find, through Rick Kelley's concert programme (https://archive.org/details/talisman1977west).

title: Shirley Chisholm closed the Black Awareness Symposium
body: Congresswoman Shirley Chisholm cancelled her February lecture, which is why the former Black Awareness Week was stretched across the spring semester as a symposium, and her rescheduled talk on 18 April closed it. She spoke on America's unfulfilled legacies before a crowd of about 250, predominantly black, who shouted and chanted in response, describing herself as a people's politician who could not be manipulated and saying she was there to tell people what they did not want to hear. The same yearbook records that lectures and concerts had been run by Associated Student Government until a reorganised University Center Board took them over in the autumn of 1979.

src.label: Talisman 1979, Black Awareness Symposium and lectures sections

why: Cut Van Meter, the 8 p.m. start, the word free and the claim that she filled the hall, all absent from the source, and cut the Herald's wording about cancelling all February appearances; added the sourced note on who ran lectures, since the symposium itself was coordinated by the university programs office.

title: ASG president shot in the members' assassination game
body: ASG members spent the autumn of 1986 playing an assassination game with squirt guns, sponsored by the congress's public relations committee. President Tim Todd was shot at about 8 p.m. on Thursday 2 October in his State Street apartment, wearing only a bathrobe. Kathryn Michelsen killed three other congress members the same night, including a sleeping Holger Velastegui, and three more on the Sunday, two of them in front of their girlfriends; she led the field until Gamaliel freshman Janet Dyer shot her between the eyes near the university center on the night of 8 October.

src.label: College Heights Herald 62:13, 9 Oct 1986 - Jessie, "Associated Student Government Members All Wet From Playing with Guns"

why: Reassigned the Sunday killings from Janet Dyer to Kathryn Michelsen, dated Dyer's shot to the night of 8 October, corrected toy guns to squirt guns and added the public relations committee as sponsor.

title: A bill to set up a Coach for a Game fundraiser
body: Bill 92-03-S, written by Mistianna Holcomb and sponsored by the public relations committee, proposed a Coach for a Game programme alongside the President for a Day event ASG already sponsored in the fall. It would have made it mandatory for every ASG member to sell ten raffle tickets at 50 cents each, with the proceeds going to a philanthropic cause. The document carries no introduction, reading or voting dates, so the file does not show when or whether it passed.
money: raffle tickets 50 cents each, ten per member

src.label: SGA Records, Bill 92-03-S, Establishment of a Coach for a Game Program

why: Cut Ralph Willard, the Central Florida game, the 29 February date, the Downing University Center ticket tables and hours, the drawing, Holcomb's job title and her quote, none of which are in the bill, and demoted the date to year only because the bill is undated.

title: $2,250 of organizational aid split between thirteen groups
body: Bill 94-2-S, introduced on 1 March 1994, disbursed the $2,250 budgeted for organizational aid after the committee spent more than four hours across three meetings deciding between the applicants. Phi Beta Sigma took $350; Alpha Phi Omega, Campus Crusade for Christ and Delta Sigma Theta took $250 each; Beta Alpha Psi $200; the Fellowship of Christian Athletes $150; the Association of Resident Assistants, the Legion of Veterans, Students' Right to Life and United Student Activists $125 each; and the International Club, SOTA and the Topperettes $100 each. It passed on second reading on 8 March 1994.

src.label: SGA Records, Bill 94-2-S, Organizational Aid Recipients

why: Swapped the two amounts the checker found reversed, giving Phi Beta Sigma $350 and the Topperettes $100, and set out all thirteen grants in full so the figures add to $2,250.

title: SGA billed Dialogue Day at Java City
body: SGA's website announced on 26 October 2003 that Dialogue Day would be held the following Tuesday, 28 October, at Java City near the library from noon to 2 p.m., where students could meet WKU administrators including their deans. The surviving capture is the notice only; it does not report on the event afterwards.

src.label: WKU SGA news page, 26 Oct 2003 (Wayback capture)

why: Recast as what SGA announced rather than what happened, and cut the unsupported claim that it became a fixture repeated in later years; I read the whole capture and the later items never mention it again.

title: Campus safety walk found nearly 30 lights out
body: SGA's campus safety walk took place in the week before 10 November 2010. Reporting to the Senate, executive vice president Kendrick Bryan said participants had found nearly 30 lights that were out around campus.

src.label: College Heights Herald, 10 Nov 2010 - Stunson, "SGA invites regents to Dine with Decision Makers"

why: Cut Mike Wallace, John Osborne and the 26 October date, which came from a pre-event notice, and demoted the day because the cited article dates the walk only to the previous week.
